All human societies follow certain rules when assigns tasks that are appropriate for each gender.� These rules for  correct gender roles vary from one society to the next. In modern industrial societies, the gender division of labor for household duties varies from family to family.� In peasant or tribal societies, the division of labor by gender is usually dictated by a list of do s and don ts.


Let s visit a husband and wife in a primitive Bushman society.� Their harsh environment makes it very important that each person follow his or her role obligations.� To move away from their organized division of labor could put their survival at jeopardy.

Wife's Duties Husband's Duties

cares for the children

build the family shelter

prepares the food

collects wood and water

keeps the fire burning

keeps the camp clean

make ornaments

collects roots and fruits

hunts animals

makes clothing form skins

makes weapons & fire sticks

starts the fire

makes large wooden containers

twists ropes

You can see how these activities are interdependent and reciprocal.� Each person has a clear understanding of what duties are expected of each one according to gender.

Here are some interesting examples illustrating cultural variations in tasks assigned to men ans women.

Hopi People:� � � � � � � � � � � Women do house building and house repairs.� Men spin and weave cloth to make the clothing for men and women
Navajo People:� � � � � � � � � � � � � Men weave ceremonial garments.� Women do the everyday spinning and weaving
Zulu Tribe: Women work in the fields, planting and harvesting the grain.� Men look after the cattle
Nuer Tribe: Men herd the cattle.� Women are the only ones who are allowed to milk the cattle

These examples show that gender roles are not explained by physical differences of the sexes.� Many roles are assigned arbitrarily to each gender by their culture. � In some cultures strong beliefs enforce the gender decisions. �

In our society we are gradually breaking away from the strict division of roles.� Women seem more flexible about breaking barriers and moving into areas of work that were once considered for  men only .� However, for the most part, men are more reluctant to assume new tasks that were once viewed as  women s work .� To answer this, we must look at the concept of status.

In North American society, the status of men has always been higher than that of women.� How a society determines the status of gender is still a mystery.� It is not based on a contribution to survival, as that is either a shared role, or in many cases, the women s role.� In some societies the status of both genders is approaching equality. In others, men are dominant.

Two universal rules seem to apply to all cultures.� The raising of infants mostly is the specialty of women, while the primary police or military force is provided by men specially trained to use weapons.� Outside of these principles, there are many variations on gender specific roles.
